text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The U.N. General Assembly will approve on Friday a resolution that calls on Israel to pay more than $1.7 million for damage resulting from its shelling of a U.N. base at Qana, in south Lebanon last year in which about 100 civilians taking refuge were killed.
- President of the World Bank James Wolfensohn who arrived in Beirut on Sunday said the bank will award Lebanon a $1 billion loan.

- Former Prime Minister Hoss denounced the U.S. position towards voting on a U.N. committee resolution that asked Israel to pay Qana damages. Only Israel and the United States voted against the resolution while Japan, Russia and Ukraine abstained.
- The Labour leader Abou Rizk was freed after eight days of arrest but still has to face charges for claiming to head Lebanon's divided labour movement.
- Prime Minister Hariri said the public school teachers salary payments and the interest on treasury bills are behind the budget deficit increase.
- The trial of five Japanese Red Army guerrillas starts today.
- The five-nation group monitoring the ceasefire in Lebanon started a meeting on Sunday to discuss two complaints of breaching a ceasefire understanding, one from Lebanon and the other from Israel.

- A Lebanese commercial delegation makes a visit to Iraq, This is the second visit of a Lebanese business delegation to Iraq in less than one month though there are no diplomatic relations between Lebanon and Iraq.
